newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan rejects China charge over fisherman's death.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan rejects China charge over fisherman's death.

text.p: Taiwan's defence ministry on Wednesday rejected charges by China that Taiwan soldiers had opened fire at mainland fishermen in two separate incidents, killing one of them.
"It was unlikely that our soldiers would open fire at fishermen, not to mention killing one of them," a ministry spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
Taiwan servicemen are under orders not to fire at fishermen, he said.
Beijing has alleged that Taiwan soliders stationed within sight of the mainland's east coast shot at the fishermen.

In a February 3 letter to Taiwan's quasi-official Straits Exchange Foundation, Beijing's Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait charged that Taiwan military "randomly shoot at mainland fishermen" and demanded a halt to such practices.
The two organisations represent the interests of Taipei and Beijing in the absence of formal links across the Taiwan strait.
China's letter, a copy of which was made public, said one incident occurred near Taiwan's defence outpost of Kinmen on January 26. A fisherman was shot in the leg.
The incident in which the fisherman was killed took place near Taiwan's other main defence outpost, the island of Matsu, the letter said.
The ministry spokesman said careful checks with the Kinmen and Matsu defence commands turned up no such incidents but he pledged a further inquiry. "We will double check," he said.

Taiwan's Straits Exchange Foundation on Wednesday reiterated its call for China to resume semi-official talks, which Beijing suspended in mid-1995, infuriated by a visit by Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui to the United States.
"This is a normal way to resolve disputes," a foundation official told Reuters by telephone.
Beijing has said Lee's U.S. trip was an attempt to promote Taiwan's independence and a move away from its advocacy of eventual reunification with the mainland.
China, which has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, has warned it would attack if the Nationalist-ruled island moved to break officially from the mainland.
